verses.text: After Hezekiah had faithfully done all these things, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He camped outside the walled towns and planned to capture them.
Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and planned to attack Jerusalem.
So he talked with his officials and military leaders about blocking off the water from the springs outside the city, and they helped him.
Many people gathered and blocked all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. They said, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?"

Hezekiah worked hard to rebuild all the broken parts of the wall and built towers on it. He built another wall outside it and made the supporting terraces in the City of David stronger. He also made many weapons and shields.
He put army commanders over the people and gathered them in the open square at the city gate. He encouraged them, saying,
"Be strong and brave. Do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and the huge army with him. The one with us is greater than the one with him.
He only has human strength, but we have the LORD our God to help us and fight our battles." The people were encouraged by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
Later, while Sennacherib king of Assyria and all his army were attacking Lachish, he sent his officers to Jerusalem with a message for Hezekiah king of Judah and all the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
It said, "Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What are you trusting in, that you stay in Jerusalem while it is surrounded?
Hezekiah is tricking you, so you will die of hunger and thirst. He says, 'The LORD our God will save us from the king of Assyria.'
Didn't Hezekiah himself remove the LORD's hilltop shrines and altars? Didn't he tell Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship at only one altar and burn incense on it'?
Don't you know what my ancestors and I have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of those nations able to save their land from me?
Not one of the gods of the nations my ancestors destroyed could save his people from me. So how could your God save you from me?

Don't let Hezekiah fool you or mislead you like this. Don't believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save his people from me or my ancestors. How much less will your God save you from me!"
Sennacherib's officers said even more against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah.

The king also wrote letters insulting the LORD, the God of Israel, and speaking against him. He wrote, "The gods of the other nations did not save their people from me, and the God of Hezekiah will not save his people from me either."
His officers shouted in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall. They wanted to scare them and frighten them so they could capture the city.
They talked about the God of Jerusalem as if he were like the gods of the other peoples of the world, which are only things made by human hands.
King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this and cried out to heaven.

The LORD sent an angel who wiped out all the strong soldiers, the leaders, and the commanders in the camp of the king of Assyria. So Sennacherib went back to his own land in shame. When he went into the temple of his god, some of his own sons killed him there with a sword.
So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from Sennacherib king of Assyria and from all their other enemies. He gave them peace on every side.
Many people brought gifts to Jerusalem for the LORD, and valuable gifts for Hezekiah king of Judah. From then on, all the nations respected him greatly.
Around that time Hezekiah became sick and was about to die. He prayed to the LORD, and the LORD answered him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah was proud and did not show thanks for the kindness he had received. So the LORD was angry with him and with Judah and Jerusalem.
But then Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem humbled themselves and turned from their pride. So the LORD's anger did not come on them while Hezekiah was alive.
Hezekiah had great wealth and honor. He built treasure rooms for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable things.
He also built storehouses for grain, new wine, and olive oil, stalls for all kinds of animals, and pens for flocks.
He built towns for himself and had huge numbers of flocks and herds, because God had made him very rich.
It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper spring of the Gihon and sent the water straight down to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah was successful in everything he did.
But when the leaders of Babylon sent messengers to ask him about the amazing sign that had happened in the land, God left him alone to test him, to see everything that was in his heart.
Everything else Hezekiah did, and his acts of faithful love, are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Hezekiah died and was buried on the hill where the tombs of David's descendants are. All the people of Judah and Jerusalem honored him when he died. His son Manasseh became king after him.
